options.label: Verse, lift, chorus (no riser build)

options.label: 8-bar loop blocks, drums drop out every third block
options.what: Drill, trap and afrobeats: one 2- or 4-bar loop under the whole song, the energy made by taking drums and bass out and putting them back. Hooks and verses alternate in 8-bar blocks; an 8-bar block with no drums every third block resets the ear.
options.how: Loop the melody; mute the kick and 808 for one block, or keep only hats; open and close with the melody and the vocal alone. Fills (a drum-fill sample, a riser, a gunshot impact) mark the block edges.

options.label: The whole song at club tempo, each pass a different job
options.what: Every sung line of the record in its own order, sped up to the style's standard tempo, with the functions turned from pass to pass: verse 1 rides the groove, chorus 1 is sung over a break with the bass out and lifts into a drop of the record's own hook, verse 2 moves into a second break, chorus 2 is sung on the drop beat, a two-bar breath, then the last hook drop. No riser builds: an empty bar before each drop does the lifting, so the drops need not be louder than the groove. A short club edit for open-format DJs (the studied one runs 2:39).
options.how: Groove: kick and bass alone for 8 bars, then claps and off-beat hats. Breaks: the bass out, a lighter syncopated kick, rolling 16th hats. The bar before each drop: everything out but a noise sweep and the last sung words. Drop after chorus 1: the hook for 8 bars, then 8 bars with a new chord layer and the bass filter closed.
